subject: Hosted API latency measurement window & p50/p95 commitment — exception request
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@olivetech.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@olivetech.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify measurement window for p50/p95 in hosted API SLA

Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement is pushing for explicit p50/p95 latency commitments in the hosted API section of the SOW, but our security and reliability teams are worried about how p95 is measured. Our traffic is bursty (event-driven ingestion) and a strict 1-minute rolling window for p95 produces a lot of volatility — causing false SLA hits during short spikes even though overall user experience is fine.

Two questions:
1) Are you open to defining p95 on a 5-minute rolling window (or an aligned 5-minute bucket), or otherwise providing a multi-window approach (p50 on 1m, p95 on 5m)?
2) What's your minimum sample size / denominator you use for computing these percentiles? Procurement wants to avoid mis-attributing outages to measurement noise.

We'd like to avoid long legal back-and-forths — if you can send a short, concrete measurement proposal we can feed it to legal and procurement. We have an internal audit early November and need the SLO language in the Master Services Agreement before then.

Thanks,
Marco
Marco Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability, OliveTech

--
Attachment: none

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@olivetech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 19:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify measurement window for p50/p95 in hosted API SLA

Marco —

Appreciate the signal and the timeline. We can be pragmatic here; below is a short proposal you can share with procurement and legal. I copied Ben (account lead) and Marissa (SRE/product) so we can align on operational and legal constraints.

Proposed measurement approach (Hosted API):
- p50: rolling 1-minute median of request latency, aggregated per-region.
- p95: rolling 5-minute percentile computed on 5 x 1-minute aligned buckets (sliding window). In practice we compute percentiles over a 5-minute sliding window updated every minute.
- Reporting window: SLO evaluation uses a 30-day rolling evaluation period for SLA reviews and credits. Incident classification (for immediate operational escalation) uses the raw 1m/5m signals.
- Minimum sample size: if fewer than 1,000 requests/day from your account in a region, p95 will be marked as Not Applicable for that day and credits cannot be triggered. For accounts above that threshold, we use the full request sample.
- Downtime/latency exclusions: known maintenance windows, upstream provider incidents (where we have confirmed dependency outage), and traffic below the sample threshold are excluded.

We will attach a short SLO draft and a small chart showing how 1m vs 5m p95 behaves for a representative OliveTech traffic trace (attached). If that looks acceptable, Ben will coordinate the contract addendum and Marissa will confirm implementation and monitoring hooks.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm the 5-minute p95 approach is acceptable to OliveTech procurement/legal.
2) We send an SLO addendum (one page) that uses the language above and includes the sample-size gating.
3) Sign and add to the MSA before your audit date.

If there are specific regulatory proofs you need (e.g., chunked audit logs of per-minute percentiles), call that out and Marissa will scope it.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karchik@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 01:10:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: OliveTech request — p95 on 5m window (need product/legal sign-off)

Marissa / Ben / Karthik —

Heads-up: OliveTech asked for p95 calculated on a 5-minute window for the hosted API (to reduce spike-driven noise). I proposed a pragmatic gating: p50 on 1m, p95 on 5m sliding window, 30-day evaluation, and a 1,000 req/day minimum sample. OliveTech has an audit early November; they want language in the MSA.

Risks / notes:
- Hosted API is multi-tenant; our current monitoring computes percentiles at per-instance and per-region levels and can emit 1m and 5m signals. The change is primarily reporting/contract wording, not runtime behavior.
- If we promise 5m p95 we should be explicit about sampling and exclusions (maintenance, provider incidents). Legal should sign off on the exact exclusion list.
- We should avoid committing any guarantees that suggest we will prevent transient spikes — instead focus on measurement definition and credits process.

Questions for product/legal:
- Marissa: implementation effort to make 5m p95 officially reportable (alerts/dashboards + audit export). ETA?
- Karthik: can you draft the addendum language around "measurement windows" and "minimum sample gating"? Keep it tight; procurement will push on credit triggers.

If we can turn around this addendum quickly we should be fine for their audit timeline. Recommend Ben own the signature path.

Thanks — Hannah

Marco —

Thanks for the quick reply. OliveTech procurement confirmed that the 5-minute window for p95 is acceptable provided the SLO language includes: a clear definition of rolling vs aligned buckets, a minimum sample gate, and enumerated exclusions. Below is the final short-form language we will propose in the SLO addendum (attached PDF):

SLO addendum (summary):
- Definitions:
  • Latency measurement: per-request server processing time measured at the Redwood edge for each successful request.
  • p50 (median): per-region rolling 1-minute percentile (updated every minute).
  • p95 (tail): per-region rolling 5-minute percentile computed as a sliding window over the most recent five 1-minute aligned buckets (updated every minute).
- Evaluation:
  • SLOs are evaluated over a 30-day rolling period for purposes of credit calculations.
  • A minimum of 1,000 successful requests per UTC-day per region is required for an SLO evaluation to be considered valid; days below threshold are excluded from credit calculations.
- Exclusions:
  • Scheduled maintenance windows declared with >= 48 hours notice.
  • Upstream provider outages where Redwood has documented dependency failure.
  • Customer traffic below the minimum sample gate.
- Monitoring and audit:
  • Redwood will provide an audit export (CSV) of per-minute aggregated percentiles for the 30-day evaluation window upon request as evidence for SLA disputes.

Operational notes: Marissa will enable the reporting flags and attach the per-minute export to the SLO page; Ben will drive the addendum signature. We will draft the one-page addendum and circulate to OliveTech procurement by EOD.

If that matches what you need, I'll route the addendum and Ben will shepherd signatures.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
